text:
alex: Heads-up — noticed a ~18% drop in tokens/sec on nightly with FlashA v2 when KV eviction happens. Context 8k, batch mixed. Before: ~4200 tok/s, after eviction: ~3450 tok/s. Cost bump visible in $/M tokens.
jana: ugh. saw a small blip in the paged-attn bench earlier, thought it was noise. do you have a perf run + kernel selection trace?
alex: pasted quick run output:
```
model: redwood-13b-fp16
hw: a100-80gb
seq: 8192
batch: 8 mixed (prefixes 256..4096)
tokens/sec: 4200 -> 3450 when eviction
kernel-selection: fused_attn chosen initially, then paged_attn fallback after kv-evict
profile: cpu spikes during re-assemble + enqueue
```
samir: @alex that smells like KV eviction forcing recompute of KV-buffered blocks which prevents fused-attn from using the streaming path. page-fallback has higher per-token overhead.
nick: kernel selector thresholds: we currently choose fused if avg_seq_len <= 512 AND total_kv_memory <= 48MB per worker. eviction increases perceived memory pressure -> selector picks paged.
jana: we should confirm eviction frequency. can you run with KV_LIMIT=64MB vs 128MB and capture eviction counts?
alex: ran it quickly; counts:
```
KV_LIMIT=64MB -> evictions: 7 in 10k tokens
KV_LIMIT=128MB -> evictions: 0 in 10k tokens
```
Throughput:
64MB -> 3500 tok/s
128MB -> 4150 tok/s
Estimated cost $/M:
64MB -> $1.02
128MB -> $0.86
```
samir: that aligns. two mitigation paths:
- adjust kernel selector bias to prefer fused_attn when majority of batch are short prefixes (even if kv memory close to limit)
- improve eviction policy to avoid mid-request evictions (delay eviction until request boundary)
- add a fast-path that retains small KV blocks for fused kernel

nick: quick microbench: applied selector bias patch (favor fused if >=75% short seqs) — results:
```
no-bias: 3500 tok/s
bias-on: 4020 tok/s
```
jana: nice. cost went down accordingly (approx $0.90 -> $0.78/M). can we run stability tests? need to ensure we don't OOM on pathological workloads.
alex: also saw a regression in one nightly where the selector logic flipped because eviction timestamp check used ms vs s. that triggered spurious memory_pressure=true. filed a bug and hotfix candidate.
perf-bot: [regression] nightly/2026-03-16 build-5533 flagged: tokens/sec median drop 15% (tagged eng-runtime)
samir: plan:
1) run full microbench matrix (KV limits 32/64/128, batch mixes 50/50/100 short) — make perf table
2) add selector unit tests + fuzzer for eviction timing
3) small rollout: enable bias on Canary group (10% traffic) + realtime token-econ dashboard
nick: can someone open a PR with the selector change and the eviction-time fix? add documentation notes (why bias exists) and add a perf-test in CI.
alex: I'll open the PR and include the bench script + numbers. also adding an opt-in config flag for private deployments since enterprises may prefer no bias.
jana: one more ask: add a KV-eviction metric to console (evictions/sec and avg re-encode time) — will help correlate cost alerts.
alex: agreed. tagging @eng-runtime and @observability for follow-up. :eyes: :thumbsup:
